headline: Bar and tavern density leads Ward 44, while park acres per resident trail the city.
summary:
Lake View and part of Lincoln Park make up Ward 44. Citywide, it sits sixth out of fifty wards this year, with an overall score of 60.13. Top marks cluster around city responsiveness and a dense bar and tavern scene. The ward finishes first on how fast the city closes routine 311 requests, first on the city's environmental justice index, and first on both the count of highly rated bars and the rate of licensed taverns per resident. Street and alley lighting soaked up more of Ward 44's aldermanic menu budget than any other project category last year, 41.6 percent of the total.

The weaker measures land in two areas, park space and religion. Ward 44 finishes last of all fifty wards on park acres per resident and last on a measure of reviews for local worship spaces. It also finishes last on several modeled estimates of religious belief and attendance, projections built from national survey data rather than a local count of who attends services.
reading_the_rankings: Park space is the clearest case. Ward 44 finishes last at 0.73 acres per 10,000 residents, but half of Chicago's fifty wards land inside an eleven-point band on this measure, so last place mainly means a crowded bottom, not a rare gap. Worship engagement, counted from Google reviews of local religious buildings, puts Ward 44 last too, though that number tracks who has claimed an online listing more than who actually attends. A thin count here could just mean fewer nearby congregations have gotten around to a page. The four religion measures behind that, covering weekly attendance, strength of belief, and certainty about God, all rank Ward 44 last as well. None of those four numbers come from asking anyone in Ward 44 a question. Each one is stitched together from how people nationwide with a similar mix of age, income and household type tend to answer, and every one of those four carries the same low confidence grade from its source.

news.headline: Lakeview High-Rise Proposal Moves Forward With Design Changes, Demolition Timeline
news.note: Developers revised a proposed 355-unit apartment tower near Diversey Harbor after six months of meetings with Ald. Bennett Lawson's office, with demolition of the vacant Stone Medical Center site set to begin next month.

news.headline: Ann Sather Taking Over Stella's Diner In Lakeview
news.note: The Lakeview restaurant chain Ann Sather is taking over the former Stella's Diner space, a sale its owner says was in the works for months before Stella's closed over health code violations.

news.headline: Mumford & Sons Kept Wrigleyville Up Late — Triggering Fines — But Neighbors Say They Didn't Mind
news.note: A weather delay pushed a Mumford & Sons concert at Wrigley Field past its scheduled cutoff, triggering fines under the city's noise ordinance, though neighbors said late shows come with living next to the stadium.

news.headline: Wrigleyville Neighbors Demand Changes To Cubs Parking Lot Expansion
news.note: Neighbors met with the Cubs and the offices of Ald. Bennett Lawson and Ald. Angela Clay to push for landscaping, stormwater, and lighting conditions on a planned parking lot expansion near Wrigley Field.
